subject: chemistry
title: Gas Pressure
welcome_lead: Inflate a balloon and the air pushes back from the inside. That push is pressure.
meta_desc: Understand gas pressure using the particle model in this KS3 chemistry adventure.
final_note: You can now explain gas pressure with particles hitting walls.

concepts.def: Force from particles colliding with a container's walls.
Each particle bumping a wall creates a tiny push.
More gas in same space = more collisions = higher pressure.
Faster particles = harder, more frequent hits = more pressure.
Less room = more collisions per second = more pressure.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Gas pressure is caused by particles smashing into the inside walls of their container. Each tiny collision pushes the wall outward.

Many collisions = pressure.

1) Add more gas — more particles, more hits.
2) Heat the gas — faster particles, harder hits.
3) Make the container smaller — particles hit walls more often.

Pumping up a bike tyre increases the number of air particles inside. A sealed drink bottle left in a hot car can burst as the pressure rises.

Even Earth's atmosphere presses on you all the time!
